cases.description: Own-widget value supplied to callback args at widget construction, without a loop or closure.

checks_performed: User reports repeating the example in a fresh tab

cases.user_message:
On Streamlit 1.64.0 with Python 3.13.0 on Ubuntu 24.04 and Firefox 143 I run this complete example. When I change Shade from Amber to Teal the selectbox shows Teal but remembered still shows Amber. I repeated that in a fresh tab. How should the callback get the new Shade value?

```python
import streamlit as st
st.session_state.setdefault("shade", "Amber")
def remember(value):
    st.session_state["remembered"] = value
st.selectbox("Shade", ["Amber", "Teal"], key="shade",
             on_change=remember, args=(st.session_state["shade"],))
st.write(st.session_state.get("remembered"))
```

hits.excerpt:
When a user interacts with a widget, the widget is updated and triggers a rerun in the following order:

1. The widget value in `st.session_state` is updated.
2. The callback function (if any) is executed.
3. The page reruns with the widget command returning its new value.

If the callback function displays anything on the screen, that content will appear above the rest of the page. A callback function runs as a _prefix_ to the script run. Consequently, that means anything written via a callback function will disappear as soon as the user performs their next action. Widget commands should generally not be called within a callback function.

<Note>

If a callback function is passed any args or kwargs, those arguments will be established when the widget command is called, not later when the user interacts with the widget. In particular, if you want to use a widget's value in its own callback function, you can't pass that value to the callback function via the `args` parameter; you must assign a key to the widget and look up its value using `st.session_state` _within the callback function_.

I am checking this design on Streamlit 1.64.0 and Python 3.13.0 on Ubuntu 24.04 with Firefox 143. The callback receives the key and looks up Session State inside the callback. Is this the right way to get the newly selected value or must I pass st.session_state["shade"] through args instead? No failure is being reported.

```python
import streamlit as st
def remember(widget_key):
    st.session_state["remembered"] = st.session_state[widget_key]
st.selectbox("Shade", ["Amber", "Teal"], key="shade",
             on_change=remember, args=("shade",))
st.write(st.session_state.get("remembered"))
```

cases.user_message:
On Streamlit 1.64.0 with Python 3.13.0 on Ubuntu 24.04 and Firefox 143 I deliberately want the callback argument to be the value from when this widget was constructed. The callback then reads the current value from Session State so I can compare old and new. For a change from North to South I want comparison to contain ("North", "South"). I am asking whether that construction-time snapshot design is valid and I am not reporting a failure.

```python
import streamlit as st
st.session_state.setdefault("direction", "North")
def compare(old_value):
    new_value = st.session_state["direction"]
    st.session_state["comparison"] = (old_value, new_value)
st.selectbox("Direction", ["North", "South"], key="direction",
             on_change=compare, args=(st.session_state["direction"],))
st.write(st.session_state.get("comparison"))
```
